segments.content:
Chapter 221-0218 Great Hero Chen Can Also Make It into 'Yi Lin'

Sichuan University.

Xu Haibo, a good boy in high school, remained a good boy in university. A cadre in the Student Union, a prospective Party member, the Youth League Secretary of his class... he seemed even more outstanding than he had been in high school.

What was even more bizarre was that he was still growing taller in his freshman year, shooting up a full 5 centimeters in one year.

"For now, you've only been identified as a candidate for development. There will be intensive training next week. Remember, guard against arrogance and rashness, and unite with your classmates."

"Thank you, Teacher!"

Xu Haibo left, delighted.

If all went well, he would become a probationary Party member by the end of this semester.

After dinner, Xu Haibo took his books and headed to the Student Union office. He would be on duty and study at the same time.

Last semester, he was just an officer, on duty every few days.

After the leadership change this spring semester, he had unexpectedly become a vice-director. Now he only went on duty occasionally, acting as the supervisor for the shift, guiding the freshman officers on how to do their work.

"Director Xu, you're here so early?" an officer greeted him.

Xu Haibo smiled and said, "You were even earlier."

After a bit of small talk, Xu Haibo sat down to read, preparing for the next day's classes.

Before long, another officer arrived.

This person wasn't on duty tonight; he had purely come to the office to hang out and build a good relationship with Vice-Director Xu.

"Director Xu, have you seen the news?" this officer asked.

Xu Haibo asked in return, "What news?"

"ByteDance got another round of venture capital. It's now valued at over two hundred million US dollars!" the officer said.

Many people at Sichuan University knew that Xu Haibo and Chen Guiliang were classmates.

This wasn't because he was showing off, but because when Chen Guiliang had just started his business, Xu Haibo had actively helped promote Xiaonei. The earliest batch of Xiaonei users at Sichuan University had been developed by Xu Haibo.

At the time, he had sent out the website URL through QQ and email, and he'd even played the friendship card: "This is my classmate's website, why not register? It's really fun!"

There was an old computer in the Student Union office. It was a bit slow, and the officer on duty was currently chatting on QQ.

Xu Haibo walked over and said, "Log into Xiaonei and take a look."

The webpage took half a minute to respond, but it finally loaded. Even before logging in, he saw the celebratory banner on the homepage.

The officer on duty muttered, "Awesome!"

The officer who had come to hang out said, "That's fucking awesome. I did the math this afternoon. Chen Guiliang's personal shareholding is worth 148 million US dollars. That's almost 1.2 billion RMB!"

"1.2 billion?" The officer on duty was dumbfounded.

The other officer said, "A little over 1.1 billion."

"Holy shit!"

"Chen Guiliang is definitely the richest university student in China."

"If I were Director Xu, I'd go work for ByteDance after graduation."

Xu Haibo took out his phone, wanting to call Chen Guiliang to congratulate him.

But after some thought, he didn't dial the number. He figured Chen Guiliang must be very busy today. Moreover, it seemed as if their pure, old friendship had undergone some kind of change because of money.

This change had already appeared during the Series A financing.

Their old classmates still discussed Chen Guiliang in private and occasionally joked about him. But fewer and fewer people actively contacted Chen Guiliang.

It was as if a rift, a distance, had formed.

After much hesitation, Xu Haibo sent Chen Guiliang a text message: "Congratulations."

A minute or so later, Chen Guiliang replied: "Haha, thanks. When are you coming to Beijing to hang out? Me and Xie Sao Bang will arrange everything."

"Maybe after graduation." Xu Haibo smiled as he typed. He felt that Great Hero Chen was still the same Great Hero Chen.

The two officers leaned in to look at his phone. "Texting President Chen?"

Xu Haibo turned off his phone screen, picked up his own textbook, and said, "You guys carry on with your duty. Call me if there's anything you can't handle."

With that, Xu Haibo slipped away.

His current dorm was a six-person room, with three computers inside. One of them was a second-hand one that Xu Haibo had picked up for only 800 yuan.

A roommate was using his computer to play *Sanguosha*.

It wasn't that he didn't want to play *World of Warcraft*, but that this old computer couldn't run it.

Xu Haibo sat down next to his roommate and said, "I need to use the computer after this round."

"Soon," the roommate said. "The Monarch is about to be killed."

The other two roommates who had computers were playing *Crazyracing Kartrider*, their bodies swaying with the turns on the track.

"Bobo, I logged into Xiaonei earlier and saw that your high school classmate got another round of venture capital," said one roommate as he drove his kart across the finish line, releasing the keyboard to rub his wrists.

Xu Haibo said, "I just found out too."

The roommate playing *Sanguosha* equipped the Sky Piercer and scored a triple kill on the Monarch and a Loyalist, then ended his turn and said, "I wonder how much Youxi Kexue is worth. *Sanguosha* must be really profitable too. He's a true legend, with two companies. Not to mention, he designed all these *Sanguosha* cards himself."

Just as he was speaking, another Rebel dealt the finishing blow, finally killing the Monarch.

That roommate got up and gave up the computer. Xu Haibo immediately sat down and logged into his Xiaonei and QQ accounts.

The high school class group chat was flashing nonstop; his old classmates were already deep in conversation.

Xu Haibo scrolled up through the messages. Due to the excessive number of unread messages and the slow speed of the old computer, the QQ group chat window was frozen for over a minute.

He finally scrolled up to the conversation from that afternoon:

"Did anyone see the celebratory announcement on the Xiaonei homepage?"

"Saw it. Great Hero Chen is so awesome!"

"What's going on?"

"Go see for yourself."

"Holy crap. A net worth of over 100 million last year was already insane, and this year it's over a billion?"

"Is Wu Meng here?"

"Here."

"Do you still live downstairs from Great Hero Chen?"

"Yeah."

"Does Great Hero Chen drive a Lamborghini to class now?"

"How could he drive a luxury car on campus? He always rides a bicycle."

"Wu Meng, help me rip Great Hero Chen off for a big meal! Make him treat us to a feast!"

"OMG. I just logged into Xiaonei to grab a parking space, and the first thing I saw was the celebratory announcement. So awesome!"

"Xie Yang is a senior executive at ByteDance now, right? Does he have shares too?"

"I think he has stock options."

"If I'd known, I would've dropped out to join Great Hero Chen. I might be a millionaire by now."

"Xie Sao Bang, hurry up and show yourself!"

"You little rascal, have some respect. You have to call him Director Xie now, you know? Director Xie, are you still looking for a lackey?"

"Not looking for a lackey, just a girlfriend. Zhang Dong, I remember your sister is very pretty. Hehehe."

"Get lost. My sister's only in her first year of high school."

"Wow, Director Xie has appeared."

"Xie Sao Bang, hurry up and get Great Hero Chen on here."

"He's not at the company. Probably in a media interview."

"So much excitement today?"

"Teacher Liu is online too. Teacher Liu, Chen Guiliang got another round of venture capital. His net worth is over 1.1 billion RMB. And that's not even counting his game company."

"Is that for real?"

"Absolutely. There's a financing announcement on the homepages of both Xiaonei and Kaixin."

"Then I have to go inform the principal."

Xu Haibo carefully read through the group chat history. Only after finishing did he type: "Great Hero Chen is simply invincible!"

As he was typing, Principal Yan from No. 2 High School was on the phone with Chen Guiliang.

After seeing this year's Gaokao cohort off, Principal Yan would be leaving the school to become the deputy county head in charge of science, education, culture, and health.

Principal Yan first congratulated Chen Guiliang, then very tactfully asked if it would be possible to invite Chen Guiliang back to the county for an event.

Chen Guiliang said he probably wouldn't have time, but he was willing to donate 100,000 yuan out of his own pocket to his alma mater to set up a grant to help students from poor families.

This was already a very sincere gesture.

Chen Guiliang's personal donations came mainly from the royalties for *Those Things About the Ming Dynasty*.

After finishing the call with Principal Yan, he called his cousin-uncle, Feng Tao, to donate 30 computers to his junior high alma mater for computer education. These computers would all be assembled by Feng Tao, which meant his cousin-uncle would also make a profit.

The promise to donate money to pave the village road also had to be fulfilled, also with personal funds. About 300,000 yuan should be enough. If that wasn't enough, he could ask the town to apply for supplementary funds. He was certain they could get special funds from the "Every Village Access" program.

Many rural villages were trying to find ways. As long as they could raise more than half of the funds themselves, there was a high chance of successfully applying for "Every Village Access" grants.

In Chen Guiliang's memory, each family had contributed a few hundred yuan, and the cement road in the village was paved around next year or the year after. The funding gap had been filled by a grant the town helped apply for.

Some villages were not united, and the farmers were unwilling to contribute money. Those had to wait in line, with some being delayed for as long as a decade. Of course, if it dragged on that long, the villagers indeed no longer needed to pool funds.

News about ByteDance's massive financing round began to be reported on major websites the next day. As for print media, apart from the daily newspapers, it would be delayed by several days.

Those reporters, as expected, used "China's Bill Gates" as a gimmick.

They said Bill Gates started his business at 20, while Chen Guiliang had a net worth of over 1 billion yuan at 20.

It caused a huge sensation in society!

Especially in Beijing, the daily, evening, morning, business, and metropolitan papers were all reporting on it in detail. Even the old uncles and aunties knew that a student had become a tycoon.

The taxi drivers in Beijing would ramble on about it to any passenger they picked up, even claiming they had once given Chen Guiliang a ride.

The cover story for the current issue of *China Youth* magazine was originally set to be Liu Tianxian. Now, it was changed to Chen Guiliang at the last minute.

On the cover, Chen Guiliang wore a T-shirt, and the lead-in headline read: A 20-Year-Old Internet Nouveau Riche.

The entire report was over twenty thousand words long, detailing Chen Guiliang's life from his childhood to the present. Much of the content was drawn from reports by various media outlets over the past two years.

This article was reprinted by dozens of media outlets, though they mostly just quoted parts of it or condensed the content and passed it off as their own reporters' work.

The venture capital funding ByteDance received this time was 2 million US dollars less than Oak Pacific Interactive. But the level of attention was not on the same scale at all.

Because Chen Guiliang was too young!

People were always more interested in so-called "child prodigies."

It even got to the point where people started to invent chicken-soup-for-the-soul stories about Chen Guiliang and submit them to magazines like *Reader*, *Yi Lin*, and *Youth Digest*.

For example, the latest issue of *Yi Lin* wrote that Chen Guiliang was so poor in high school that a rich classmate mocked his ragged clothes and laughed at him for often collecting trash to sell to the recycling station.

Chen Guiliang didn't retort, only writing in his diary: Even in a pile of scraps, wings that soar can grow. Knowledge is gold that never depreciates. I must study hard to become a useful person.

It wasn't until he got into Peking University that Chen Guiliang said to that classmate: "Life may give me barren soil, but it cannot kill my desire to grow upwards. Hardship is not a medal, but it has tempered and strengthened my resolve."

Many high school students who read the *Yi Lin* article actually believed that Chen Guiliang had made a living by collecting trash in high school. And they used this as material for their Gaokao essays this year...

(End of this chapter)
